entity_title: Guest Worker permit — no eligible nationalities
fact_text: Under Government Decree No. 450/2024, there are currently no third countries whose nationals may be employed in Hungary under a residence permit for guest workers. An employer-sponsored professional cannot use the Guest Worker route and must instead qualify for the Hungarian Card, EU Blue Card or residence permit for the purpose of employment.
evidence_quote: there are no third countries whose nationals may be employed in Hungary under a residence permit for guest workers

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the 'Guest Worker' permit is the general route for foreign workers. Actually, as of the 23 December 2024 decree no third country's nationals qualify for it. Action: route employer-sponsored professionals through the Hungarian Card or EU Blue Card, never the Guest Worker permit.

fact_text: Family members of a third-country national who holds (or is applying for) a residence permit for the purpose of employment may not be granted a residence permit for family reunification. The basic employment permit does not open a family-reunification route.
evidence_quote: an applicant for a residence permit for the purpose of employment may not be granted a residence permit for family reunification

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any work-based residence permit lets a spouse and children join. Actually the plain 'residence permit for the purpose of employment' explicitly bars family reunification. Action: for employees relocating with dependants, confirm a permit type that permits family reunification before filing rather than the basic employment permit.

entity_title: Employment permit — no in-country switch of purpose
fact_text: While holding, and even after the expiry of, a residence permit for the purpose of employment, an application for a residence permit under another legal title (a different purpose) is not allowed within Hungary. Changing residence purpose means re-applying from abroad.
evidence_quote: application for the issuance of a residence permit under another legal title is not allowed in Hungary

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can switch to a family, study or other permit from inside Hungary once settled. Actually employment-permit holders may not lodge an application for another purpose within Hungary. Action: plan any change of residence purpose as a fresh application filed at a Hungarian consulate abroad.

fact_text: The Hungarian Card, for third-country nationals with higher professional qualifications, is issued for a maximum of 3 years and may be extended for a further 3 years.
evidence_quote: The validity period of the document is maximised in 3 years, and it may be extended for 3 years

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a highly-skilled work permit grants long, open-ended residence. Actually the Hungarian Card is capped at 3 years, extendable by 3, and differs from the EU Blue Card's 4-year term. Action: diarise the renewal well ahead of the 3-year expiry.

entity_title: Apply at a Hungarian consulate abroad
fact_text: If entry to Hungary is not visa-exempt, the residence-permit application must be submitted outside Hungary, before a Hungarian diplomatic or consular mission in the applicant's country of nationality or habitual residence. A separate visa application is not required, as the residence-permit application includes the visa to collect it.
evidence_quote: You may submit an application before a diplomatic or consular foreign mission of Hungary in the country of your nationality or your habitual place of residence

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can enter Hungary and then sort out the work/residence permit locally. Actually a visa-required third-country national must file the residence-permit application at a Hungarian consulate abroad first. Action: build consulate lead time into the relocation before the employee travels.

entity_title: Type D visa to collect the permit
fact_text: Once a residence-permit application filed abroad is approved, the Hungarian consulate issues a type D visa to enter Hungary and collect the residence permit. It is a single-entry visa authorising a stay of not more than 30 days and valid for 3 months.
evidence_quote: type D visas entitling their holder to receive their residence permits issued to third-country nationals are single-entry visas authorising a stay of not more than 30 days and are valid for 3 months

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the approved residence permit itself is what you travel on. Actually you first receive a single-entry type D visa (max 30-day stay, valid 3 months) to enter and pick up the permit card. Action: enter Hungary within the visa window and collect the residence permit.

entity_title: Single permit is tied to the named employer
fact_text: Hungary's single permit is one residence permit that both authorises residence and entitles the third-country national to a contract employment relationship with the specific employer indicated on the permit; work authorisation and residence are combined in one employer-tied document.
evidence_quote: A single permit is a residence permit that entitles a third-country national to establish contract employment relationship with an employer indicated on the permit

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work visa lets you work for any employer. Actually the single permit ties work authorisation to the one employer named on the permit. Action: treat any change of employer as requiring a new or extended permit before the employee starts the new job.

entity_title: EU Blue Card — changing employer needs a new application
fact_text: If an EU Blue Card holder wants to change employer, has their legal relationship terminated, changes job, or takes on additional part-time work, they must submit an application for the extension of the EU Blue Card via the Enter Hungary platform, regardless of how many years they have worked in Hungary.
evidence_quote: you will be required to submit an application for the extension of your EU Blue Card via the Enter Hungary platform, regardless of how many years you have been working in Hungary

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed that after some years an EU Blue Card holder can freely change jobs. Actually any employer or job change requires a fresh EU Blue Card extension application on Enter Hungary, no matter the tenure. Action: file the extension before switching employer or adding a second job.

entity_title: EU Blue Card — minimum salary threshold
fact_text: For 2025, the minimum monthly earning required for an EU Blue Card in Hungary is HUF 883,671 (a lower figure applies to certain listed healthcare occupations). The applicant must prove income at this level to qualify.
evidence_quote: in 2025, the minimum amount of earning per a month specified in relation to EU Blue Cards is HUF 883,671

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any professional salary qualifies for the EU Blue Card. Actually there is a specific statutory minimum monthly wage (HUF 883,671 in 2025) the offered salary must meet. Action: confirm the offered gross monthly salary clears the current EU Blue Card threshold before filing.

entity_title: Hungarian tax ID via form T34
fact_text: A foreign private individual with taxable income in Hungary must request a tax identification number (adoazonosito jel) from the tax authority (NAV) using form T34, after which NAV issues a tax card. The residence-permit data is also made available to NAV on the same form.
evidence_quote: he/she must request a tax identification number from the competent tax authority using form T34

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a Hungarian tax number is issued automatically with the residence or work permit. Actually the individual must proactively apply to NAV using form T34 to obtain the tax identification number. Action: file NAV form T34 on arrival, before the first payroll run.

entity_title: Register accommodation within 3 days of entry
fact_text: After entering Hungary a third-country national must register their accommodation, and any later change of accommodation, within 3 days on the electronic immigration case-management platform (Enter Hungary).
evidence_quote: must register his/her accommodation or any change of accommodation after his/her entry (within 3 days) on the electronic immigration case management platform

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the address on the application is enough and there is nothing to do on arrival. Actually accommodation (and any move) must be registered within 3 days of entry via Enter Hungary. Action: register the Budapest address on Enter Hungary within 3 days of landing, and re-register after any move.

fact_text: If the third-country national does not enter Hungary within 3 months from the date the residence permit's issuance was approved and does not start the approved residence, the approved residence permit becomes invalid and the accrued right of entry and residence ceases.
evidence_quote: if you do not enter the territory of Hungary within 3 months from the date of approval of the issuance of your residence permit and do not start your approved residence

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an approved residence permit can be picked up whenever convenient. Actually you must enter Hungary and begin residence within 3 months of approval or the permit lapses. Action: schedule the move so the employee enters within the 3-month window after approval.
